highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159 previews Skia m159 with programmable GPU meshes and an experimental image-comparison package.
highlights_body: This line also corrects Windows image-decoding crashes, runtime-effect uniform initialization, and Apple device frameworks. WebAssembly now requires .NET 9 or later, and Linux x86 native assets are no longer packaged.

breaking.title: Move WebAssembly apps to .NET 9 or later
breaking.body: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp no longer provide .NET 8 WebAssembly native assets; unsupported WASM targets are rejected during the build. Retarget WebAssembly apps to .NET 9 or later and use the matching runtime assets. Non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support is unchanged.

breaking.title: Move Linux x86 deployments to a supported architecture
breaking.body: Linux x86 native assets are no longer built or included in NuGet packages for SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp. Move 32-bit Linux deployments to a supported architecture, such as x64 or ARM64, before upgrading.

bullets.detail: Updates the native renderer to m159, bringing WebAssembly SIMD CPU rasterization and Windows font-loading improvements. Subsequent m159 fixes harden mask-filtered glyph reloads, correct image-filter cache-key equality, and work around Imagination Vulkan descriptor-allocation failures without changing the milestone.

SKMeshSpecification, indexed and non-indexed mesh builders, vertex/index buffers and SKCanvas.DrawMesh expose custom SkSL vertex and fragment programs. Built meshes retain their native dependencies after the source wrappers are disposed. Drawing requires a GPU-backed surface; raster drawing is a no-op.

SkiaSharp.Testing adds SKImageComparison for images, bitmaps and pixmaps, with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets, error metrics and difference images. The separate package is experimental: acknowledge diagnostic SKIA4001 to opt in. Returned comparison results retain no native handles; difference images belong to the caller.

Fixes process termination during libjpeg/libpng longjmp error recovery in x64 clang-built natives, including malformed JPEG decoding and PDF output with lazy non-JPEG images. Control Flow Guard remains enabled; x86, ARM64 and MSVC builds are unchanged.

New SKRuntimeEffectUniforms blocks now start at zero rather than containing leftover memory. Reset clears the existing buffer in place, avoiding a native buffer and managed wrapper allocation on each call; the fix also covers mesh uniforms.

bullets.lead: Filtered texture edges and Tizen blurs
bullets.detail: Ganesh sampling clamps slightly inside texture subsets to avoid undefined exterior texels; CPU and Graphite sampling are unchanged. Tizen now applies its intended CPU blur-path selection when compiling Skia. Texture-edge pixels and Tizen blur output or performance may differ; Tizen performance was not measured.

bullets.lead: Correct iOS and tvOS device frameworks
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp device frameworks now contain only arm64 device binaries and device platform metadata, avoiding the simulator slices and metadata that could trigger App Store error ITMS-90087. Separate simulator frameworks and their x64/arm64 slices remain available.
Replaces the string-path Window binding with a typed expression, removing the trimming warning when constructing SKGLView in trimmed MAUI apps without changing the binding's intended behavior.

contributor_summaries.taublast: Zero-initialized runtime-effect uniforms, allocation-free buffer resets and test snapshot disposal.
contributor_summaries.bhall-ctre: Trim-safe Window binding for MAUI SKGLView.
contributor_summaries.kdpkke: Correct iOS and tvOS device-framework packaging while preserving simulator slices.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored the Uno Gallery and its views projects to the Windows sample solution.
contributor_summaries.SimonCropp: Windows x64 libjpeg/libpng error-recovery crash fix.

preview_summaries.v4.159.0-rc.2.26576.7: Release Candidate 2 adds experimental SkiaSharp.Testing image comparisons, zero-initialized runtime-effect uniforms and trim-safe MAUI SKGLView binding. It also fixes Windows x64 image error-recovery crashes, adjusts Ganesh texture sampling and Tizen CPU blurs, and removes Linux x86 native assets.
preview_summaries.v4.159.0-rc.1.26567.13: Release Candidate 1 adds programmable GPU mesh drawing and corrects SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp iOS/tvOS device frameworks. It also incorporates glyph-rendering, image-filter cache and Imagination Vulkan allocation fixes.
preview_summaries.v4.159.0-preview.1.26563.22: Preview 1 introduces Skia m159, including WebAssembly SIMD CPU rasterization and Windows font-loading improvements. WebAssembly apps now require .NET 9 or later; non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support is unchanged.

harfbuzz_summary: HarfBuzzSharp now requires .NET 9 or later for WebAssembly and no longer packages Linux x86 native assets. Its iOS/tvOS device frameworks now contain only arm64 device slices and the correct device metadata, while separate simulator frameworks remain available.

v4.159.0-preview.1.26563.22.headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 Preview 1 introduces Skia m159 with WebAssembly SIMD rasterization and Windows font-loading improvements.
v4.159.0-preview.1.26563.22.body: WebAssembly consumers now require .NET 9 or later; non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support is unchanged. HarfBuzzSharp package revision 15.0.0.100 retains native HarfBuzz 15.0.0.

v4.159.0-rc.1.26567.13.headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 Release Candidate 1 adds programmable GPU mesh drawing.
v4.159.0-rc.1.26567.13.body: Custom SkSL mesh programs support indexed and non-indexed geometry on GPU-backed surfaces; raster drawing is a no-op. This candidate also corrects SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp iOS/tvOS device frameworks and incorporates glyph-rendering, image-filter cache, and Imagination Vulkan allocation fixes.

v4.159.0-rc.2.26576.7.headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 Release Candidate 2 adds experimental image-comparison APIs and fixes Windows x64 image-decoding crashes.
v4.159.0-rc.2.26576.7.body: The new SkiaSharp.Testing package provides configurable comparisons and difference images. This candidate also zero-initializes runtime-effect uniforms, removes the MAUI SKGLView trimming warning, adjusts Ganesh texture-edge sampling and Tizen CPU blurs, and stops packaging Linux x86 native assets.
